items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: One of the few lead pianos I ever played with, Paul.

ctx.x: Said he played over there. I used to play over there with Brownlee too at Thomas East, right out of Harvey. Every Saturday night. You talk about a hot spot. That was it. And we used to play at the Red Top Inn in Gretchen. That was a bar with Brownlee. We'd come back sometime after the Thomas East would break up with Gil going in. Played just with the bars, you know. This Norman Brownlee was a regular guy.
Do you know him, Dan? Yeah, I know him. I went to Pensacola.

Fine, fine. He's very nice. Yeah. And he was a good counterman. Still is. I'm hurting him lately. He sat down with Raymond and me when we were there with Al Marico in 1958. Came in. He still sure plays good. Yeah, he used to be. Well he played a lead piano. One of the few lead pianos I ever played with, Paul. He knew tempos and when he'd set a tempo, man it was wonderful.
